If users keep complaining, consider: (a) parallelizing comment posts with multiple browser tabs/contexts, or (b) restoring an opt-in API path for users who can provide an Adobe-IMS token. Acknowledge the 'one range comment quirk' (1/8 comments at t=6 became a 0:06 → 0:10;07 range comment). Probably because the playhead crossed onto a selection-modifier state during the multi-step seek. Low priority — main agent already accepted this as a known quirk.

critical_code_review_comments: frameio_service._seek_forward relies on keyboard shortcut timing (Shift+ArrowRight ~0.333s, ArrowRight ~1/30s). If Frame.io ever changes their key bindings (or A/B tests UI variants), every comment will land at frame 0 again silently. Add a defensive post-seek verification: read the current timecode label/badge from the DOM and assert it's within ±0.5s of target before posting; if mismatched, log a warning and skip the comment instead of posting at the wrong place.

Comments are sorted by timestamp ASC so we 'only seek forward' — but there's no reset between comments. If a seek overshoots (Shift+ArrowRight is 0.333s, so for a 0.1s gap to next comment we'd overshoot), the next forward step lands further past target. Verify by computing achieved-vs-target offsets and logging them in the pipeline report so we can tune the step granularity.

Range-comment quirk (1/8 at t=6 became a 4-second range) suggests the playhead-focused element accidentally entered a 'range selection' mode (likely Shift held too long bridging two seeks). Consider releasing Shift between coarse and fine steps explicitly via page.keyboard.up('Shift').

POST /api/analyses still returns analysis.model_dump() including the raw 'password' field on creation (server.py:351) — strip happens only on GET. Low risk in guest mode but defense-in-depth fix is trivial.
_run_pipeline still has no overall asyncio.wait_for timeout; a hanging Playwright session could occupy the worker indefinitely (carried over from iter 7).

rca of the issue: BUG (resolved): All Frame.io comments were anchored to frame ~14. RCA: prior implementation set HTMLMediaElement.currentTime via JS, which moves the underlying <video> element but does NOT update Frame.io's React player state — the comment composer reads its anchor from Frame.io's internal player state, so every comment got posted at whatever value that state held (the default ~frame 14). Fix: focus [data-testid=playhead] (the actual Frame.io slider DOM node) and dispatch keyboard events that Frame.io's player listens for — Shift+ArrowRight for coarse 0.333s steps and ArrowRight for fine 1/30s steps. Comments are sorted ASC by timestamp_sec so seeks only go forward. Reproduction (pre-fix): post 2+ comments at different DB timestamp_sec values via the old pipeline → on Frame.io's share UI, all show at the same anchor. Verification (post-fix, current): analysis ca520f74 has issues at DB ts {0.0, 2.0, 6.0, 8.0} AND on the actual Frame.io share they show at corresponding TCs (visually confirmed by main agent via /tmp/verify_comments.py).
